What percentage of India's disease burden is linked to unhealthy diets, according to ICMR-NIN's 2024
guidelines?
options: Nearly 100%
About 5%
About 56.4%
About 10%
questions.explanation: ICMR-NIN's 2024 guidelines estimate that around 56.4% of India's total disease burden is linked to unhealthy diets.

questions.question: Why does the body need fibre as part of a balanced diet?
options: It has no real digestive function
It only affects taste, not health
It should be avoided in most diets
It supports healthy digestion and helps maintain steady blood sugar levels
questions.explanation:
Fibre supports healthy digestion and helps maintain more steady blood sugar levels, making it an important part of a
balanced diet.

questions.question:
Why might front-of-pack nutrition labelling be considered especially helpful for consumers with lower literacy
levels?
options: Because simplified visual labels can convey key nutrition information more quickly than dense text-based panels
Because front-of-pack labels are purely decorative with no informational value
Because literacy level has no bearing on how labelling should be designed
Because only highly literate consumers benefit from any food labelling
questions.explanation:
Simplified, visual front-of-pack labels can convey key nutrition information more quickly and accessibly than dense text-
based nutrition panels.

questions.question: What recent step did the Supreme Court direct FSSAI to take regarding food labels?
options: Ban all packaged food
Implement simple, front-of-pack nutrition labels
Remove all labelling requirements
Allow unregulated health claims
questions.explanation:
In 2026, the Supreme Court directed FSSAI to implement simplified front-of-pack nutrition labelling for easier consumer
understanding.

questions.question: What best describes an 'ultra-processed food'?
options: Fresh, unprocessed vegetables
Whole grains with no additives
Industrially manufactured food, often high in sugar, salt, or fat
Home-cooked meals only
questions.explanation: Ultra-processed foods are industrially manufactured, often containing high levels of sugar, salt, or unhealthy fats.

questions.question:
Why is 'cooking at home more often' associated with better control over nutrition, according to healthy living
guidance?
options: Because home cooking guarantees perfect nutrition regardless of ingredients used
Because restaurant food is always nutritionally superior
Because home cooking has no bearing on ingredient choices
Because cooking at home allows more direct control over ingredients, portions, and added salt, sugar, or fat
questions.explanation:
Cooking at home gives a person more direct control over ingredients, portion sizes, and how much salt, sugar, or fat is
added.

questions.question: What is the main function of protein in the body?
options: Builds and repairs muscles and tissue
Regulates body temperature only
Provides quick energy only
Has no real biological function
questions.explanation: Protein is essential for building and repairing muscles and body tissue.

questions.question: Why does JSSK specifically cover transport costs in addition to medical procedures?
options: Because transport has no bearing on a mother's ability to access institutional delivery
Because removing transport as a financial barrier helps ensure mothers can actually reach a facility for safe delivery
Because JSSK only covers costs after delivery, not before
Because transport costs are unrelated to maternal health outcomes
questions.explanation:
Covering transport costs removes a practical financial barrier that might otherwise prevent a mother from reaching a
facility for safe delivery.

questions.question:
Why does general guidance suggest involving the 'whole family' in health planning rather than relying on one
person?
options: Because only one family member should ever be responsible for health matters
Because family involvement has no bearing on health outcomes

Because preparedness and awareness are more resilient when shared across the family rather than depending on one
individual
Because relying on a single person is always the most effective approach
questions.explanation:
Sharing health awareness and responsibility across the family makes preparedness more resilient than depending on just
one individual.

questions.question:
Why might 'Ayushman Arogya Mandirs' be particularly relevant to women's health awareness and elderly care
simultaneously?
options: Because they are exclusively for maternity care
Because they only serve one specific age group
Because they have no connection to preventive screening

Because they offer free primary care and screening accessible to family members across different life stages, including
women and the elderly

As primary care centres, Ayushman Arogya Mandirs offer free screening and care accessible to family members across
different life stages, including both women's health and elderly care needs.

questions.question: What is CHILDLINE's helpline number in India?
questions.explanation: CHILDLINE, India's free 24x7 helpline for children in distress, can be reached at 1098.

questions.question:
Why does the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 include provisions for old age
homes?
options: Because this provision is unrelated to elderly welfare
Because the Act aims to ensure support options exist for elderly citizens who may lack adequate family care
Because old age homes have no legal basis in India
Because all elderly citizens are legally required to live in old age homes
questions.explanation:
The Act ensures support options like old age homes exist for elderly citizens, particularly where adequate family-based
care may not be available.

questions.question: Which nutrient need increases significantly during adolescence, especially for menstruating girls?
options: Artificial sweeteners
Caffeine
Iron
Trans fat

Keeping medicines and cleaning products out of children's reach
questions.explanation: Keeping medicines and hazardous products out of children's reach is a fundamental home safety measure.

Only adult vaccination
Corporate employee wellness
Senior citizen pensions

Pregnancy
Adolescence
Old age

options: They are only open to adults
They exclusively handle emergency surgeries
They offer a comfortable, confidential space for adolescent health questions
They are only available online
questions.explanation:
Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics offer a comfortable, confidential environment designed specifically for adolescent health
needs.

questions.question:
Why might a family with a newborn and an elderly grandparent living together need to adapt multiple parts of
their health routine at once?
options: Because newborns and elderly individuals have identical health requirements
Because adapting routines for multiple life stages is unnecessary
Because only one member's needs ever matter at a time
Because each life stage present in the household has distinct needs that benefit from simultaneous, tailored attention

When multiple life stages are present in one household, each brings distinct needs that benefit from simultaneous, tailored
attention rather than a single generic approach.

questions.question: What is a key nutritional priority for senior citizens?
options: Adequate protein, calcium, and Vitamin D
Avoiding protein entirely
Only consuming sugary foods
Eliminating all dairy products
questions.explanation: Senior citizens benefit from adequate protein, calcium, and Vitamin D to support muscle and bone health.

questions.question:
What is a practical benefit of maintaining a shared 'family health folder' containing vaccination records and
insurance details?
options: It is only useful for tax purposes
It allows quick, confident access to important information during unexpected situations like a sudden hospital visit
It has no practical use during a medical emergency
It replaces the need for any actual medical care
questions.explanation:
A shared family health folder allows quick, confident access to important records, which is especially valuable during
unexpected situations like a sudden hospital visit.

questions.question: Why might a family's 'one-size' meal plan fail to serve every member well?
options: Because variety in meals is unnecessary for good health
Because meal planning has no connection to health outcomes
Because nutritional needs vary meaningfully by life stage, such as pregnancy, childhood, or old age
Because all family members have identical nutritional needs
questions.explanation:
Nutritional needs vary meaningfully across life stages, meaning a single meal plan rarely serves every family member
optimally.

questions.question:
Why does child safety guidance recommend teaching children about 'safe and unsafe touch' in general,
protective terms?
options: Because this topic has no relevance to child safety
Because children should be given explicit details about specific incidents
Because this guidance is only relevant to law enforcement, not parents
Because general, age-appropriate awareness helps children recognise and report concerning situations to a trusted adult
questions.explanation:
General, age-appropriate awareness helps children recognise concerning situations and know to tell a trusted adult,
supporting their safety without requiring explicit detail.

questions.question:
Why does family health guidance recommend keeping vaccination and health records organised and accessible
to the whole family, not just one member?
options: Because shared access ensures continuity of care even if the primary record-keeper is unavailable
Because only one family member should ever need this information
Because organising records has no practical benefit
Because records only matter for legal purposes, not health
questions.explanation:
Shared access to health records ensures continuity of care and informed decision-making, even if the usual record-keeper
isn't available.

questions.question: Why is exclusive breastfeeding recommended for the first 6 months of an infant's life?
options: Because it has no nutritional relevance at all
Because it provides complete, appropriate nutrition for early infant growth and development
Because this recommendation applies only in rural areas
Because formula is always superior for the first 6 months
questions.explanation:
Exclusive breastfeeding provides complete, appropriate nutrition tailored to an infant's needs during the critical first 6
months of growth.

questions.question: Why does bone health guidance emphasise childhood and adolescence rather than focusing only on elderly care?
options: Because childhood nutrition has no connection to adult bone strength
Because bone health is entirely irrelevant until old age
Because peak bone mass built during youth significantly affects fracture risk and bone health in later life
Because bone density is fixed at birth and cannot be influenced later
questions.explanation:
Since peak bone mass is built in youth, early nutrition and activity significantly influence bone strength and fracture risk
decades later.

questions.question:
A teenager seems reluctant to discuss physical changes with parents. What does RKSK-aligned guidance
suggest?
options: Assume no support is needed since they haven't asked
Avoid the topic permanently
Force the conversation regardless of their comfort
Keep the conversation open and non-judgemental, and mention adolescent-friendly clinics if needed
questions.explanation:
Maintaining an open, non-judgemental approach, while mentioning available resources like adolescent-friendly clinics,
respects the teenager's comfort while keeping support accessible.

questions.question: Why might 'women's health awareness' specifically emphasise regular screening, even without symptoms?
options: Because several women's health concerns can be detected earlier through regular screening, improving outcomes
Because symptoms always appear early enough for effective treatment
Because screening is only relevant for older women
Because screening has no diagnostic value without symptoms
questions.explanation:
Regular screening can detect certain health concerns earlier, even before symptoms appear, improving the chances of
effective treatment.

questions.question:

options: Because hiding it has historically improved health outcomes
Because reframing it this way helps reduce stigma and supports girls' confidence and school attendance
Because menstruation has no biological basis
Because this framing has no practical impact on behaviour

Framing menstruation as normal and healthy helps reduce stigma, which in turn supports girls' confidence, comfort, and
school attendance.

Exclusive breastfeeding
Solid food only

This issue is unrelated to school attendance
All girls attend school without any menstruation-related impact

access gap.

questions.question: Why might 'geriatric care' differ meaningfully from general adult healthcare?
options:
Because ageing introduces specific health considerations, such as increased fall risk and chronic disease management, that

Because elderly individuals have identical healthcare needs to younger adults
Because ageing has no distinct health implications
Because geriatric care is simply a rebranding with no real difference
questions.explanation:
Ageing introduces specific considerations, such as increased fall risk and chronic disease management, that justify a more
focused geriatric care approach.

options: Care focused exclusively on infants
Medical care specifically focused on the health needs of older adults
Care that only applies in emergency situations
General care with no age-specific focus
questions.explanation: Geriatric care refers to medical care specifically focused on addressing the health needs of older adults.

questions.question: Why might a family reconsider a grandparent's home safety after a minor fall, even if no serious injury occurred?

Because home safety is unrelated to fall history
Because even a minor fall can indicate a hazard or vulnerability that could lead to a more serious incident later
Because falls in elderly individuals are never a cause for attention

questions.question: Why might 'active and healthy ageing' be a more accurate framing than assuming decline is inevitable with age?

Because decline is entirely unavoidable regardless of any intervention
Because ageing always leads to complete physical decline with no exceptions

Because many aspects of health can be maintained or improved through activity, social engagement, and preventive care,
even in older age

Many aspects of health can be maintained or improved in older age through continued activity, social engagement, and
preventive care, challenging the assumption that decline is inevitable.

Foreign healthcare consultants
Private hospital administrators

questions.question: What does JSY encourage among pregnant women?

Institutional delivery through cash assistance
Avoiding all medical checkups
Home delivery only

Seeking a medical review promptly

Free eyeglasses
Free bicycles for girls
Biodegradable sanitary pads at ₹1 each

Because family health always takes care of itself without any effort

questions.question:

Because a single annual review covers all necessary precautions permanently
questions.explanation:
Since health risks shift meaningfully with the seasons, a recurring reminder helps ensure precautions are updated
appropriately throughout the year.

questions.question: A family packs a travel health kit only for long-distance trips, not shorter ones. Why might this be reconsidered?
options: Because short trips never require any health-related preparation
Because unexpected health needs can arise on any trip, regardless of distance, making basic preparation broadly useful
Because travel health kits are only legally required for international travel
Because health risks are exclusively tied to distance travelled, not trip type
questions.explanation:
Unexpected health needs can arise on any trip, making basic travel health preparation broadly useful, not just for long-
distance travel.

questions.question: Why is 'portability' relevant to a family relocating or travelling between Indian states?
options: Because portability has no connection to healthcare access
Because health scheme benefits are always restricted to one specific hospital
Because portability refers to the ability to use a health scheme's benefits across different states or hospitals
Because portability only concerns physical luggage while travelling
questions.explanation:
Portability refers to being able to use health scheme benefits, like Ayushman Bharat, across different states or empanelled
hospitals.

questions.question:
Why is noting local emergency numbers for a travel destination useful, in addition to saving home-area
numbers?
options: Because emergency numbers are always identical across every state
Because only international destinations require separate emergency numbers
Because local numbers are never actually needed while travelling

Because some emergency services or specific numbers can vary by location, making destination-specific awareness
valuable
questions.explanation:
Since some emergency services or specific numbers can vary by state or region, knowing destination-specific numbers
adds an extra layer of readiness while travelling.

questions.question:
Why does this module suggest treating the Final Health & Emergency Checklist as something to revisit every few
months, not complete once?
options: Because circumstances, family composition, and readiness can change over time, requiring ongoing review
Because the checklist becomes legally invalid after one use
Because revisiting a checklist repeatedly has no practical value
Because a single completion is always sufficient for permanent readiness
questions.explanation:
Since circumstances and family needs can change over time, treating the checklist as an ongoing, periodically revisited
tool ensures continued readiness.

questions.question: Why does this module recommend printing or saving checklists somewhere visible, like a fridge or noticeboard?
options: Because checklists are only effective if kept completely hidden from view
Because visibility increases the likelihood that checklists are actually used and followed consistently
Because visible placement has no bearing on whether a checklist gets used
Because printed checklists are illegal to display in Indian households
questions.explanation: Keeping checklists visible increases the likelihood that they are actually referenced and followed consistently in daily life.

questions.question:
Why does this module recommend reviewing checklists on a set schedule rather than only when a problem
arises?
options: Because checklists are only useful after a problem has already occurred
Because scheduled review has no real advantage over reactive checking
Because regular review helps catch issues before they become emergencies, rather than after
Because reactive checking is always more effective than proactive review
questions.explanation:
Regular, proactive review helps catch potential issues before they escalate into emergencies, rather than only reacting
after a problem arises.

questions.question:
Why does seasonal health guidance recommend removing stagnant water specifically before and during
monsoon season?
options: Because removing stagnant water is purely a cosmetic practice
Because stagnant water has no connection to disease risk
Because this precaution is only relevant during summer
Because stagnant water is a breeding ground for mosquitoes that spread diseases like dengue and malaria
questions.explanation:
Stagnant water serves as a breeding ground for mosquitoes, making its removal an important precaution against dengue
and malaria, especially during monsoon.

questions.question:
Why might 'the best emergency plan is the one you never had to use' be an appropriate way to frame the value
of preparedness?
options:
Because it suggests good preparedness aims to prevent or minimise harm, even if the plan itself is never dramatically
tested
Because this phrase has no real connection to the purpose of preparedness
Because this statement implies preparedness plans are ultimately pointless
Because emergency plans are only valuable if they are frequently needed
questions.explanation:
This framing suggests that good preparedness aims to prevent or minimise harm — success can mean the plan quietly
worked, not that it was dramatically tested.

questions.question:
Why does seasonal precaution guidance specifically recommend monitoring elderly family members during
winter?
options: Because this recommendation applies equally to all age groups with no special elderly focus
Because elderly individuals may be more vulnerable to cold-related respiratory illness, warranting closer attention
Because monitoring elderly family members is only relevant during summer heatwaves
Because winter poses no additional risk to elderly individuals specifically
questions.explanation:
Elderly individuals can be more vulnerable to cold-related respiratory illness during winter, making closer monitoring a
valuable precaution.

questions.question: Why should medicines be stored out of children's reach?
options: Because storage location has no bearing on child safety
Because this has no real safety benefit
Because it helps prevent accidental ingestion and poisoning in children
Because medicines never pose any risk to children
questions.explanation: Storing medicines out of children's reach helps prevent accidental ingestion, which could otherwise lead to poisoning.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to keep emergency numbers written on paper, not just saved in a phone?
options: Because digital numbers are illegal to use in emergencies
Because paper copies replace the need for calling entirely
Because paper copies are always more accurate
Because phone batteries can fail exactly when they're needed most
questions.explanation: A written copy ensures access to emergency numbers even if a phone's battery fails during a critical moment.

questions.question: Which number appears on the Emergency Contact Checklist for poisoning-related emergencies?
questions.explanation: 1800-116-117, the National Poisons Information Centre, is listed on the checklist for poisoning-related emergencies.

questions.question: What should a basic travel health kit include?
options: Nothing beyond a phone charger
First aid essentials and regular medications
Extra electronics with no medical relevance
Only souvenirs
questions.explanation: A basic travel health kit should include first aid essentials and any regular medications a traveller needs.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to drink only sealed or trusted water sources while travelling?
options: Because bottled water always tastes better
Because sealed water has no real safety benefit
Because it reduces the risk of waterborne illness from unknown water quality
Because this recommendation only applies outside India
questions.explanation: Drinking from sealed or trusted sources reduces the risk of waterborne illness from water of uncertain quality.

questions.question: What does the Home Safety Tips checklist recommend regarding fire readiness?
options: Avoiding any fire-related equipment at home
Storing fire equipment in a locked, inaccessible cupboard
Relying solely on neighbours during a fire
Keeping a working fire extinguisher or fire blanket accessible
questions.explanation: Keeping a working fire extinguisher or fire blanket accessible is part of the recommended home safety checklist.

questions.question:
Why does family preparedness guidance recommend that at least one adult in the household know basic first aid
and CPR?
options:
Because having this knowledge readily available within the household can be critical during a genuine emergency before
professional help arrives
Because only healthcare professionals are ever expected to know first aid or CPR
Because first aid and CPR knowledge has no bearing on family emergency outcomes
Because this knowledge is legally required for all Indian citizens
questions.explanation:
Having at least one household member trained in basic first aid and CPR can be critical during the minutes before
professional help arrives.

questions.question:
Why might 'checklists are only useful for beginners' be specifically challenged using examples from aviation and
surgery?
options: Because aviation and surgery are entirely unrelated to general health checklists

Because even highly experienced professionals in these fields rely on checklists to prevent avoidable errors, showing
checklists remain valuable regardless of expertise
Because expertise always eliminates the need for any structured checklist
Because these fields never actually use checklists in practice
questions.explanation:
Even highly experienced professionals in fields like aviation and surgery rely on checklists, demonstrating that expertise
doesn't eliminate the value of structured, repeatable safety steps.

questions.question: Which number should be included in every family's emergency contact checklist for unified emergency response?
questions.explanation: 112 is India's unified emergency number and should be included in every family's emergency contact checklist.

questions.question:
Why might 'reassessing travel health preparation before every trip, not just long-distance ones' be considered
good practice?
options: Because only long-distance trips carry any health-related risk
Because reassessment before every trip has no real practical benefit
Because travel health kits should only be assembled for international travel
Because even short trips can present unexpected health needs, making consistent preparation a valuable habit
questions.explanation:
Even short trips can present unexpected health needs, making consistent preparation before any trip a genuinely valuable
habit.

questions.question: Why should a home first aid kit be checked periodically rather than assembled only once?
options: Because items can be used, expire, or become outdated over time
Because a first aid kit should be discarded after one use regardless of contents
Because periodic checks have no practical value
Because kits never need any maintenance once assembled
questions.explanation: Since items can be used, expire, or become outdated, periodic checks help ensure the kit remains genuinely ready for use.

questions.question:
Why might this module be considered a fitting conclusion to the entire Health & Emergency Awareness category,
rather than an entirely separate topic?
options: Because it introduces entirely new topics unrelated to earlier modules
Because it consolidates practical action from across all previous modules into a single, reusable, everyday system
Because it repeats each earlier module's content in full detail
Because concluding modules should always be unrelated to what came before
questions.explanation:
This module consolidates practical action from across all previous modules into a single, reusable, everyday checklist
system, making it a fitting conclusion to the category.

questions.question:
Why does this module's closing message emphasise having 'a system you actually follow' over simply 'knowing
everything'?
options: Because systems and knowledge are functionally identical concepts
Because consistent follow-through has no bearing on actual safety outcomes

Because knowledge without consistent follow-through provides limited real-world protection compared to a reliably followed
system
Because knowing everything is always more valuable than having any practical system in place
questions.explanation: Official JanGyan verified citizen concept.
